hook.en: A gentle muscle contraction by the patient against your precise resistance, followed by a stretch or movement into the new range.
hook.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET) mein patient apni muscle se controlled contraction karta hai aur therapist munasib resistance deta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Muscle Energy Technique (MET) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Muscle Energy Technique (MET) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

text.en: Muscle Energy Technique (MET) uses the patient's own muscle effort. They push lightly in a specific direction against your counterforce for several seconds, then relax, and you take the joint or muscle to a new end of range.
text.ur: Patient apni marzi se muscle contract karta hai aur therapist controlled resistance deta hai, taake range, tone aur movement tolerance par kaam kiya ja sake.

simpler.en: A gentle muscle contraction by the patient against your precise resistance, followed by a stretch or movement into the new range.
simpler.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET) mein patient apni muscle se controlled contraction karta hai aur therapist munasib resistance deta hai.

text.en: Like a spring that has just been squeezed gently: after letting go, it stretches more easily. The patient provides the energy; you only guide direction and limits.
text.ur: Jaise spring ko halka sa dabaya jaye: chhorne ke baad woh zyada asaani se khinchti hai. Taqat patient lagata hai; aap sirf direction aur hadood guide karte hain.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Precise position, direction and gentle force (about 20 percent of maximum effort) matter more than strength.
**2.** Post-isometric relaxation: after a gentle hold, the muscle often relaxes and stretches more.
**3.** Reciprocal inhibition: contracting the opposite muscle can help the tight one relax.
text.ur: Mumkin asraat mein stretch tolerance, sensorimotor effects aur protective muscle activity mein kami shamil ho sakti hai. Post-isometric relaxation aur reciprocal inhibition aam teaching models hain, lekin clinical response ko sirf ek reflex mechanism se explain nahi kiya ja sakta. Active mobility aur strengthening ke sath integrate karna mufeed ho sakta hai.

text.en:
So when does **Muscle Energy Technique (MET)** make sense?
• Muscle tightness limiting range, for example hamstrings or hip muscles.
• Joint stiffness where a muscle contributes, such as a restricted neck rotation.
• When the patient cannot tolerate forceful stretching.
text.ur: Dard ke sath muscle guarding; restricted range; selected pelvic, spinal ya peripheral movement impairments.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Fracture, acute tear, severe osteoporosis or instability.
• Uncontrolled blood pressure problems (avoid breath-holding).
• Pain that increases with the contraction.
text.ur:
Recent muscle injury, instructions follow karne mein mushkil, ya contraction ke dauran dard.
Acute fracture, unstable joint, surgery ke baad contraction par pabandi, ya severe acute pain.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Find the restriction
steps.detail: Move the limb or joint to the first resistance. Example: raise the straight leg until the hamstring tightens.

steps.title: Choose the direction
steps.detail: For PIR, the patient pushes with the tight muscle. For RI, with the opposite muscle.

steps.title: Give clear instructions
steps.detail: 'Push gently against my hand, about a fifth of your strength.'

steps.title: Hold the contraction
steps.detail: Hold for about 5-10 seconds while you match their force so nothing moves.

steps.title: Relax and take up the slack
steps.detail: Tell them to relax fully, wait a moment, then move to the new barrier.

beats.ur:
1. Restricted movement assess karke comfortable barrier identify karein.
2. Patient ko dard se pehle wali comfortable position mein rakhein.
3. Patient se prescribed direction mein gentle isometric contraction karwayein, jabke therapist matching resistance deta hai.
4. Relaxation ke baad nayi available range ko baghair force kiye hasil karein.
5. Zaroorat ke mutabiq repeat karke reassess karein.

question.en: Imagine the patient is in front of you. What do you do FIRST?
question.ur: Farz karein patient aap ke saamne hai. Aap SAB SE PEHLE kya karenge?

feedback.en: Right — this comes first. Move the limb or joint to the first resistance. Example: raise the straight leg until the hamstring tightens.
feedback.ur: Sahi — sab se pehle yehi. Move the limb or joint to the first resistance. Example: raise the straight leg until the hamstring tightens.

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: contraction of about 20 percent effort held 5-10 seconds, 3-5 repetitions, with a short stretch hold (about 10-30 seconds) after the final repeat.
text.ur: Aam tor par 10–30% effort ke qareeb gentle contraction 5–10 seconds ke liye sikhayi jati hai. Dobara assessment se pehle aksar 3–5 cycles kaafi ho sakte hain. Dose ko patient aur response ke mutabiq adjust karein.

beats.patient: Alina, 29, runner, tight right hamstring; straight leg raise 65 degrees.
beats.assessment: Gentle stretch sensation, no sharp pain, no tear signs.
beats.treatment: At 65 degrees she presses her heel lightly into your shoulder for 8 seconds, relaxes, and you lift the leg further. Repeat 4 times.
beats.reassess: Raise improves to 80 degrees. She repeats the stretch daily and continues hamstring strengthening.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Farz karein hip movement restricted hai. Assessment ke baad therapist patient ko comfortable position mein rakh kar halki isometric contraction karwata hai. Relaxation ke baad range dobara check hoti hai. Yeh fictional example hai, har hip problem ke liye treatment plan nahi.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Asking for a hard contraction that causes shaking and pain.
• Not waiting for full relaxation before moving.
• Allowing the joint to move during the contraction.
text.ur: Patient ko breath hold karwana, excessive force demand karna ya pain ko ignore karna avoid karein. Treatment ke baad comparable range, symptoms aur functional movement ko dobara check karein; worsening response par technique modify ya stop karein.

text.en: MET can improve flexibility and short-term pain in some conditions, but the original neurological explanations are not well proven. Gains may come from changes in stretch tolerance.
text.ur: MET mobility ya symptoms mein selected patients ko help kar sakti hai, lekin har restriction ka cause muscle tightness nahi hota. Isay universal realignment technique na kahein; active exercise aur wider rehabilitation ke saath consider karein.

text.en: One line to carry into the clinic: **Light push, full relax, then move to the new barrier.**
text.ur: Zyada force behtar nahi hoti; aam tor par halka aur accurate contraction hi kafi hota hai.
